newsitem.title: GERMANY: Zeitler - Germany could meet EMU deficit goal in 97.
newsitem.headline: Zeitler - Germany could meet EMU deficit goal in 97.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler said on Tuesday that Germany had a realistic chance of meeting the government deficit target for currency union membership this year.
"I think there is a good, realistic chance that Germany will meet the deficit criteria this year," said Zeitler.

He said that meeting the proposed EMU start date of January 1, 1999 on time should not jeopardise stability in the union and added that he expected Germany to meet its 2.5 percent growth target in 1997.

Zeitler said he thought Germany had a good chance of meeting the criteria because of the high level of price stability, low interest rates and a positive environment for exports in Germany. The Maastricht treaty requires would-be members of European and Monetary Union to post budget deficits of no more than three percent of gross domestic product.
Zeitler said the proposed EMU start-date should be adhered to, but that a timely start on January 1 1999 should not be at the expense of stability.
"Nobody will move into a house which does not have solid foundations," said Zeitler.
He ruled out the use of creative accounting to help Germany meet the Maastricht goals, which he said would not inspire confidence in the euro.
The deutschemark should be the benchmark for stability for the euro, Zeitler said.
However, the euro would not be a panacea for all ills and could not take the place of discussions on bringing German competitiveness into line and domestic reform, Zeitler said.
